findings.title: Financials' trailing lens screams full price
findings.body: Financials trade at 15.45x forward estimates while its trailing P/E sits at the 98th percentile of its five-year range. The 42-point gap between lenses is the widest in the table, meaning the market is assigning very little credibility to the 28 percent earnings growth analysts project for next year.

findings.title: Real Estate's surge ignores flat earnings
findings.body: Real Estate's forward multiple jumped 40 percentile points in a month yet its implied next-12-month earnings are expected to decline 1 percent. The sector now sits at the 49th percentile from both lenses, so the repricing is purely multiple expansion with no fundamental support on the horizon.

findings.title: Information Technology now cheapest in five years
findings.body: Information Technology's forward P/E sits at the 0 percentile — the cheapest it has been in five years — after falling 18 percentile points in a month. The trailing multiple at the 20th percentile is still far above, and the 61 percent implied earnings growth suggests the market is pricing in a very sharp recovery that hasn't shown up in reported results yet.
